items.title: [Bambu Lab Community Forum - Latest posts] Foam board cutting with the H2D laser?
items.content_html:
Yes — the H2D 455 nm blue diode laser handles tool shadowboard inserts really well as long as you pick the right foam chemistry:

  1. Material choice (critical for both cut quality and machine safety):

    • Avoid PVC / vinyl foam completely — chlorine gas from PVC will corrode the H2D linear rails and optics in a single session.
    • Dark charcoal/black closed-cell EVA foam (EVA38 or EVA45 density) cuts far cleaner on a 455 nm diode laser than white or light-colored cross-linked PE (XLPE / Kaizen). Blue 455 nm light scatters inside white PE and leaves wide melted bevels, whereas black closed-cell EVA absorbs 455 nm cleanly with crisp vertical walls.

  2. Practical thickness & pass limits:

    • 10W module: Clean single-pass cuts on 5–10 mm black EVA (~650–800 mm/min, 85–90% power, air assist ON).
    • 40W module: Can step through 15–25 mm black EVA in 2–3 Z-stepped passes without heavy top-edge char if you keep speeds up and let air assist clear the kerf.

  3. CAD layout tips for calipers & hand tools:

    • Offset tool outlines outward by ~0.18–0.22 mm to compensate for thermal melt kerf so micrometers/calipers press-fit snugly instead of rattling.
    • Keep at least 8 mm foam ribs between adjacent tool pockets so walls don’t tear out, and add 18 mm semicircular finger-pull notches on flush-seated gauges.

(Full disclosure: I built a small browser tool for my own shop) If you want 1:1 tool outlines without a flatbed scanner or manual spline tracing in Fusion, you can drop your calipers or pliers on a standard A4 or US Letter sheet and run a top-down phone photo through FoamKerf — it rectifies camera tilt into a 1:1 kerf-compensated DXF/SVG (or a rigid 3D-printable STL if you ever want a hard PETG drawer insert instead).

items.title: [digitaltrends.com] Google speeds up Gemini commands in the smart home by up to 20 percent
items.content_html: Gemini for Home, Google's AI assistant for Home and Nest devices, has been answering everyday smart home commands up to 20 percent faster since November 17, according to the company. Google has now fully rolled out the speed improvement. The new features complement the Google Home app update released on November 25. Among other things, the update fixes issues with follow-up commands and stopping media. A faster version of Gemini Live conversation mode is due to arrive on speakers and displays in the coming weeks. Users will then also be able to set timers and switch lights on and off during a conversation. Google still hasn't given a firm launch date and hasn't said whether the new version will be available in German at the same time.

items.title: [Bambu Lab Community Forum - Latest posts] Bambu Lab P3C is here: Tool changer, now standard
items.content_html:
Surely, they could have made many other decisions to reduce the price, but delivering it with 2 nozzles, would not really make it competitive to the U1 or any other tool changer.

And the P3C is an answer to the U1.

It swaps tools (and therefore materials) in less than 4 seconds, but people complain about the initial loading time of the filament. It is still a hobby machine.

When you know on forehand that you constantly need to load different materials, you can always go for the U1 or another machine from the competition if you think it better. Don’t underestimate all the other hassle that comes with those machines.

It’s an entry tool changer machine with a competitive price.

And it’s pretty hard to build a one-size-fits-all solution in 3D Printing. I bet the engineers and marketers will have had many discussions over this topic for sure.

And maybe in the near future, an Automatic loading AMS will be released.

items.title: [Bambu Lab Community Forum - Latest posts] Loud Clattering/Clicking,
items.content_html:
Hello,

This is the response from Bambu Lab Support.

Dear Customer,

Thank you for your reply.

We’ve reviewed your video, and there’s nothing obviously abnormal during the manual movement. The sound isn’t coming from the idler pulley.

The sound you hear while printing is most likely caused by the toolhead starting and stopping quickly over short distances, which produces a mechanical sound as the motion absorbs the impact. This is normal and won’t affect the printer’s performance.

Because the H3C prints with higher speed and acceleration than our other models, this sound tends to be more noticeable on the H3C.

If the sound bothers you and you’d like to reduce it, there are two things you can try: 1. Turn on Silent Mode. You can switch it on directly in “Settings” on the printer’s screen, and it can effectively reduce operating noise. 2. Adjust the slicer settings. In your slicer (such as Bambu Studio), lower the maximum acceleration a little, then re-slice and print again. This can also noticeably reduce the sound.

If you still have any issues after making these adjustments, please don’t hesitate to contact us.

Best regards,
Bambu Lab Customer Support

The support team’s response isn’t entirely satisfactory, but it makes sense. The print quality is good. The only real downside: Compared to the H2C, it’s significantly louder.

items.title: [Bambu Lab Community Forum - Latest posts] Section Analysis in Bambu Studio
items.content_html:
There is no sectional (“cutaway”) view like commonly found in CAD/CAM software, if that’s what you’re thinking.

You can however scroll through each layer of the slice, from either the top or the bottom, using the scroll/zoom-like bar on the right of the slicer preview. This lets you see the insides pretty well.
Examples in the wiki: View slicing information | Bambu Lab Wiki

(There are some sort-of “sectional” views with some of the tools available in the Prepare tab, but frankly they’re all pretty useless.)

items.title: [lxer.com] CachyOS adds Easy Anti-Cheat v2 support; Fortnite expected first
items.content_html: The November release of CachyOS, an Arch-based distribution, adds support for Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) Linux v2, a game-protection system that checks a computer’s boot setup before allowing a game to start. Heise reported that no game was using the Linux v2 system yet and that Fortnite is expected to be the first. CachyOS supplies a separate signed kernel and boot option for EAC-protected games, while the standard boot entries remain available. Enabling the EAC option requires Secure Boot, a trusted signing key, TPM 2.0, an enabled IOMMU and kernel lockdown. The release also includes a redesigned package installer and a recovery environment for Btrfs snapshots.

items.title: [linuxtoday.com] Ubuntu 27.04 daily builds available ahead of April 2027 release
items.content_html: Ubuntu 27.04, codenamed “Tenacious T-Rex,” is available as daily development builds for testing ahead of the stable release scheduled for April 22, 2027. The initial images are based on Ubuntu 26.10 and include Linux kernel 7.3 and the GNOME 51 desktop. The images contain development code and are not recommended for critical day-to-day use; testing in a virtual machine or on a separate disk or partition can limit disruption. Early development is expected to focus on package syncing and lower-level updates, with desktop changes arriving later.
